contract.headline: A 48h timelock covers contract-upgrade (proxyAdmin). asset-permission (BRIDGE_ADMIN_ROLE, DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE) has NO established delay — timelock: none. The delay protects the code and not the supply.
contract.headline_basis: Derived from the layer rows below, not authored here, so it changes when the walk changes.

paths.name: LayerZero OFT adapter
paths.note: mint(address,uint256) 0x40c10f19 is AccessControl-gated on BRIDGE_ADMIN_ROLE, held by this OFT adapter, owned by OPS_SAFE. setPeer on the adapter IS a mint — same finding already recorded on susde.

paths.name: OPS_SAFE
paths.note: getRoleAdmin(BRIDGE_ADMIN_ROLE) == 0x00 == DEFAULT_ADMIN, which OPS_SAFE holds on all four chains. It can grant mint to any address in ONE transaction. Two independent routes to the same undelayed mint.

paths.name: ProxyAdmin
paths.hand_walk: Live EIP-1967 reads on USDai 0x0A1a1A107E45b7Ced86833863f482BC5f4ed82EF returned ProxyAdmin 0x2ddf39c7...aadc3c and implementation 0x0ab74df5...bc212. ProxyAdmin.owner() returned TimelockController 0x0eea1ee0...95639b; getMinDelay() returned 172800 seconds. Live hasRole checks returned GOV_SAFE as proposer, canceller, and executor, OPS_SAFE as executor, and the timelock itself as DEFAULT_ADMIN. updateDelay(0) succeeding from the timelock itself while reverting from 0x...dEaD tests the onlySelf access check, not reachability. Reducing the delay must be scheduled and executed through the current 48h delay.

paths.name: OAdapter (USDai LayerZero OFT adapter)
paths.hand_walk: Arbitrum implementation 0x0ab74df531c0d8f1c46643e404b3d14723bbc212 defines InvalidAddress() with selector 0xe6c4247b and applies onlyBridgeAdapter to mint(address,uint256); that modifier reverts when msg.sender differs from immutable _bridgeAdapter. A live simulated mint reverted with 0xe6c4247b from 0x...dEaD and succeeded from OAdapter 0xffa10065...b4bae5. The adapter's token() returned USDai, owner() returned OPS_SAFE, and endpoint() returned the LayerZero V2 endpoint. OPS_SAFE is 3-of-3 with owners 0xe982b3f6...0a69c, 0x986868c9...579b2, and 0xd1affe27...7b75e. This is an immutable adapter-caller gate, not BRIDGE_ADMIN_ROLE and not a deposit precondition.

walk_notes: ✅ HAND-WALKED, NOT GENERATOR OUTPUT. This file deliberately does NOT carry the
TRUST WARNING banner the other 27 asset files carry — those were produced by
tools/topology.py (ICED 2026-08-24, 63.5% of its rows untrustworthy). Every row
below was read directly and the load-bearing claims were verified twice: walked
by riskAnalyst 2026-08-26, then re-resolved independently here from a different
starting point before filing.
⚠️ NOT HELD. USDai appears in no wallet — checked across all per-wallet
asset_scores. This is a WATCH-ONLY observation, like hastra-prime. It carries
no severity weight until a position exists, and it stands the moment one does.
Per tools/held-flag.py: off-book suppresses weighting, never the row.
VERIFICATION TRAIL (this repo, plasma, 2026-08-26):
keccak("BRIDGE_ADMIN_ROLE") == 0x751b795d…f4bf                        MATCH
adapter 0xffa10065….owner() -> OPS_SAFE 0x5f0bc72f…5841f  3-of-3      MATCH
token EIP-1967 admin slot   -> ProxyAdmin 0x2ddf39c7…aadc3c           MATCH
ProxyAdmin.owner()          -> timelock 0x0eea1ee0…95639b  48h        MATCH
timelock RoleGranted @creation block 20,669,363, 0 failed chunks:
PROPOSER/CANCELLER/EXECUTOR -> GOV_SAFE 0x783b08aa…a07b
EXECUTOR                    -> OPS_SAFE
DEFAULT_ADMIN               -> itself (self-administered)
GOV_SAFE getOwners() == OPS_SAFE getOwners(), 3-of-3 both              CONFIRMED
⚠️ THE FINDING IS THAT THE TWO-SAFE STRUCTURE SEPARATES NOTHING. A governance
Safe and an operations Safe reading as distinct controls are the same three
keys. Recorded because no single-Safe read reveals it — it is only visible when
both owner sets are compared, and nothing in the schema prompts that comparison.
⚠️ THRESHOLD EQUALS OWNER COUNT (3-of-3), so the usual quorum caveat inverts:
every key is load-bearing, and losing one makes the timelock permanently
un-proposable. That is an availability risk, not a compromise-threshold one.
⚠️ CODEHASH COMPARISON WOULD HAVE LIED. The token is at the same address on
arbitrum/ethereum/base/plasma (deterministic deploy) but is NOT the same
bytecode: base and plasma differ in exactly 32 bytes at offset 815–846 — the
IPFS hash inside the CBOR metadata trailer. Executable bytes 0–814 are
identical, both solc 0.8.29. STRIP THE CBOR TRAILER BEFORE COMPARING.
